raw_collector_report.scope: local CLI output backpressure; no physical USB or kernel changes

local-backpressure.boundary: Only collector JSON and frozen source/sequence are archived; no independent syscall or pipe-byte raw recording for these two older cases.

boundaries: Independent offline raw parsing, no import/call of runner.verify, no Cargo/build/QEMU or repository mutation. Four physical regression sections reuse the previously reviewed independent parser with only source/run-name changes; original empty-ECM-stderr assumption was already corrected in that parser.

Reviewed five regression QEMU runs / ten guest exits, four local signal cases and two older local backpressure cases. The two new opt-in autorestore positives are reviewed separately by another agent; their PASS is not established by this report.

The default journal uses actual disk1 and IPC1, retaining null drivers and old immutable grants through helper restart; guest administrator restores, root read-only reconcile retires, third real I/O follows. No default-off automatic recovery or schema promotion occurred.

Normal/hot and TERM older collectors archive expected FTDI digest/byte assertions, not raw host FTDI sink files. Journal host105 raw bytes, journal/TERM evdev bytes, and both ECM PCAPs are independently decoded. No absent raw artifact is invented.

Four older physical regression harnesses do not independently archive per-grant disk journal records; normal wait0/stopped exercises the guarded product close-and-Finish path, but record retirement there is inferred from that path rather than directly read.

Local blocked signal cases prove process exit and two data socket EOFs with stdout still unread; terminal backend cleanup snapshot remains unobserved. The two older backpressure cases provide collector JSON, not an independently recorded syscall trace.

Only recorded Linux/QEMU synthetic devices and local virtual tests: no real hardware G1/G2, Windows support, kernel-internal active-syscall window, all-FD capability revocation or power-loss durability established.
